label: Delimiter step of short (L=3,4) or maximal-length (L=9) sequences
explanation: Fires only at the <DEL> step (phase 1, recall_idx 0); zero activation on every original-phase and copy-phase step. Within the delimiter, the firing rate depends strongly on sequence length: about 80% of L=3 delimiters, about 23% of L=4 and L=9, and only 0.2-1% of L=5-8. L=3 carries the strongest activations (37% coverage of the top quartile from L=3 alone). Which delimiters fire within a length is decided by token content in a diffuse way: it is more likely when the first original token is a letter, especially i (also a, o, f, u, v, j), and less likely when the sequence has digits, but no simple token rule captured this (adding letter or first-token conditions traded recall for precision without improving F1). The predicate (phase 1 and L in {3,4,9}) gets about 84% of activation mass but precision is only about 0.29.
